content.user_title: Animate Images into Short Videos with Magic Hour
content.value_statement: A single still image is rarely enough to produce a convincing short video, because appearance problems cannot be fixed by motion. This skill solves appearance in the start frame first, then animates the approved frame with Magic Hour and inspects the finished clip before delivery.
actual_capabilities: Plans a shot from a brief: subject action, camera move, aspect ratio, and the details that must stay fixed.
Prepares a start frame with the Magic Hour AI Image Editor or AI Image Generator tools.
Animates the approved still with the image-to-video model and a structured motion prompt.
Guides local file handoff through a presigned upload URL before generation.
Waits on image and video projects and inspects the finished clip for identity, motion, and artifacts.
Records project IDs, acceptance criteria, and credit spend so a repair reuses accepted work.
limitations: Requires a connected Magic Hour creation MCP or a Magic Hour API key.
Generation consumes paid Magic Hour credits and cannot produce free output.
Output quality depends on the source frame; image-to-video will not repair a poor still.
Multi-shot sequences are assembled with an external editor, not inside the skill.

use_cases.title: Bring a portrait to life
use_cases.description: Animate a single portrait or character still into a short clip with one controlled expression or gesture.

use_cases.title: Product reveal clips
use_cases.description: Turn a product still into a short reveal while protecting packaging, logo, and the layout of the frame.

use_cases.title: Short narrative sequences
use_cases.description: Direct a multi-shot story from approved stills and assemble the shots into one short film.

prompt_templates.title: Basic image to video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use magic-hour-image-to-video to turn my attached portrait into a five-second clip. Keep the face and clothing unchanged and add a slow push in.
prompt_templates.scenario: First-time user with one source image.

prompt_templates.title: Edit the start frame first
prompt_templates.prompt: Use magic-hour-image-to-video to change the background of my product photo to a marble counter, then animate it with a locked camera and soft steam.
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs a new composition before any motion is generated.

prompt_templates.title: Direct one specific motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Use magic-hour-image-to-video to animate my character shot. She turns slightly toward the camera and smiles. Keep the camera locked, preserve her identity, and add no cuts.
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants one precise action and reaction.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-shot sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use magic-hour-image-to-video to build a three-shot sequence from this character reference: arrival, a small discovery, then one clear action. Inspect each still before animation and save the individual shots.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user directing several beats with continuity.

output_examples.input: Animate this portrait into a five-second vertical clip with a slow push in.
output: Plan: 5 seconds, 9:16, one slow push in, identity and clothing fixed.
Start frame approved: face, lighting, and background unchanged.
Video delivered: 1080x1920, 5 seconds, no audio, first frame matches the approved still.
Image and video project IDs returned with the file.

output_examples.input: Make a product reveal from this bottle photo.
output: Still prepared: background cleaned, label and logo preserved.
Motion: locked camera, soft light sweep, held final exposure.
Inspection: label text stable, no warping, dimensions and duration verified.

best_practices: Approve the start frame before you spend credits on motion.
Describe one action and one camera move instead of restating the whole image.
Keep project IDs and acceptance criteria so a repair reuses accepted work.
anti_patterns: Resubmitting a creation call after a wait timeout.
Asking a nontechnical user for model fields or a motion-prompt template.
Chaining unreviewed edits instead of deriving every still from one approved reference.

faq.question: Do I need a Magic Hour account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill creates media through the Magic Hour creation MCP or your MAGIC_HOUR_API_KEY.

faq.question: Does generating video cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. Every image and video project consumes Magic Hour credits, so the skill checks your budget first.

faq.question: Can it animate any image?
faq.answer: It works best with a clear, well-lit source image. It will not repair a badly composed or low quality still.

faq.question: Can it make more than one shot?
faq.answer: Yes. Each shot is prepared and approved as its own still, then animated and assembled with an editor.

faq.question: What do I need to provide?
faq.answer: A source image or a description, your intended use, and a spending limit. The skill chooses the technical settings for you.

faq.question: Does it upload my files?
faq.answer: Local inputs are uploaded to Magic Hour storage through a presigned URL before generation begins.
